title: introduce-cost-simulator-snapshot-autoscaler-and-ensemble-quant-validator
author: Lina Chen
release_notes: Adds a snapshot-driven cost simulator, a deterministic autoscaler dry-run CLI, and an ensemble quantization validator. No runtime defaults changed; this is tooling and tests only.
description:
Motivation and summary: Customer and internal signals show unpredictable tenant autoscaling outcomes when cold-starts and microburst patterns hit. This PR introduces a snapshot-driven cost simulator and a deterministic autoscaler dry-run to let SRE and tenant-ops evaluate unit-econ impact before changing live defaults. In addition we add an ensemble quantization validator that runs candidate quant profiles against historical snapshots to detect regression in token-level costs and decoding latency. The goals are: 1) provide a reproducible dry-run for autoscaler policy changes; 2) make quant changes auditable with fail/pass thresholds; 3) expose per-tenant unit-econ projections to the console and CLI for faster ops decisions.

What changed (high level):
- new package: tools/costsim: simulator harness that replays snapshot traces, simulates batching/cache/quantization choices, and emits a per-tenant CSV report (unit_econ_expected_cost, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, batch_efficiency).
- new CLI: bin/redwood-cost-sim with commands: run --snapshot <file> --policy <yaml> --quant-profile <name> --dry-run --output <csv>. The CLI supports --ensemble which runs multiple quant profile candidates and summarizes deltas.
- autoscaler dry-run mode: autoscaler now accepts a --dry-run input file (simulator snapshot) and outputs recommended scale actions without touching live pools.
- quant validator: tools/quant_validator runs candidate profiles against the snapshot KV/cache state; it fails if token-cost increases > 3% or p95 latency regresses more than configured threshold.
- telemetry/metrics: added cost_sim.duration_ms, quant_validator.regressions, autoscaler_sim.action_count and debug traces for request routing decisions used in simulation.
- tests: unit + integration harness under tools/costsim/tests with sample snapshots and golden CSVs; CI integration test added to ensure the CLI returns expected exit codes and outputs in --dry-run.

Design notes and motivation: We intentionally keep the simulator deterministic: snapshots include request timestamps, token counts, KV cache state fingerprints and model selection. The replay engine applies the same scheduling and batching heuristics that the runtime uses (continuous batching, prefix-KV cache hits). This lets us compute realistic latency and token-cost deltas for alternative quant profiles without needing a full GPU cluster. The ensemble quant validator executes candidate quant profiles in a lightweight emulation path (kernel latency approximations + measured microbench numbers) and cross-checks against the snapshot trace to produce both cost and quality proxies.

Review conversation (high level):
- Marc Andre (reviewer): "Nice isolation of the simulator. Two asks: (1) make snapshots schema-stable and versioned, (2) ensure we don't accidentally ship sample snapshots with PII. Can you add a sanitizer step?"
- Lina Chen (author): "Added snapshot schema v2 and a sanitizer that strips identifying tokens in tests. Updated docs and fixtures."
- Priya Nair: "Please add an option to fail CI when quant_validator reports regressions beyond the threshold so PRs altering quant profiles are gated."
- Lina Chen: "Added a quant-validator CI job and a --strict flag for the validator. Also added a smoke test in .github/workflows/cost-sim.yml."
- Omar Velazquez: "Minor: prefer smaller CSV columns and include a JSON blob for per-route diagnostics."
- Lina Chen: "Adjusted CSV columns and included a diagnostics.json alongside CSV for deep inspection."

CI summary:
- unit tests: pass
- integration/cost-sim smoke: initially failed due to fixture PII, rerun after sanitizer fix: pass
- linting: pass
- quant-validator: pass (strict mode exercised in a staging CI job)
- e2e: skipped (not required for tooling-only PR)

Risk and rollout: Low risk, tooling-only change. No runtime default changed. The autoscaler dry-run is opt-in and requires explicit file input; no config flags are changed for production by default.

Release notes and ops instructions:
- Admins can run: bin/redwood-cost-sim run --snapshot tools/costsim/tests/fixtures/sample_snapshot_v2.json --policy tools/costsim/example_policy.yaml --quant-profile q8_0 --dry-run --output /tmp/tenant_report.csv
- To validate a quant change in CI: add a job that runs tools/quant_validator/validator.py --snapshot <fixture> --profile <candidate> --strict and fail the job if regressions detected.

Observability & Dashboards: Added a lightweight cost-sim dashboard (observability-pack) showing cost_sim.duration_ms distribution and a quant_validator.regressions timeseries.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged to main with commit message "tools: add cost simulator, autoscaler dry-run and ensemble quant validator (ENG-4321)".
